newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to wander around 20,000 line.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to wander around 20,000 line.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to wander around the 20,000 line in Wednesday trade, after the key Nikkei 225 ended higher after a fall below that support level Tuesday, brokers said. They said the market would keep a wary eye on the Iraqi situation but any impact was likely to be limited.
On Tuesday, the key 225-share Nikkei average ended up 91.04 points or 0.45 percent to 20,198.15 after slipping as low as 19,920.02. Its September futures gained 100 points to 20,250.
"The Nikkei average rebounded strongly after falling yesterday, almost too strongly," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.
"Selling pressure could set in today and lower the average," Ueki added.
Market sources said that although some oil company share prices may rise, the effect of tension in Iraq was likely to be small on the Tokyo stock market.

"The Dow weakened upon opening overnight but then firmed, which means that the U.S. markets have digested the news of the U.S. missile attack and Tokyo will not take it as a threat either," one broker said.
The Dow industrials rose 32.18 points to 5,648.39 on Tuesday in moderate trade.
